title: A hundred tokens instead of forty-two thousand
subtitle: Compiling an agent's tool catalog into a 0.6-billion-parameter model that cannot invent a tool

stats.label: recall at 5; the strongest classical baseline scored 0.949

engine memory on the card the 30B model already uses

lede: An agent connected to a serious tool estate pays for that estate on every turn. The schema of every tool it might call is loaded into context whether it uses one or not. Measured on the wire, that cost was mine on every turn. I replaced the catalog with a single discovery tool backed by a 0.6-billion-parameter model that has the catalog memorised and cannot name a tool that does not exist. The model's recall matches the strongest retrieval baseline I could build, and that tie is published beside it. Two failures, both expensive.
quote: The baseline was weak. I struck the comparison.
evidence: LLM fine-tuning for tool discovery: a 0.6-billion-parameter model fully fine-tuned on a corpus generated from the tool registry, rebuilt in minutes whenever the registry changes.
Grammar-constrained decoding: a grammar compiled from the registry and applied during decoding, so no tool name outside the catalog was produced in any run.
Context-window cost reduction for agents: an agent's whole tool catalog replaced by one discovery tool, about a hundred tokens of standing context in place of forty-two thousand.
ML evaluation methodology: recall at 5 of 0.955 against 0.949 for the strongest classical baseline I could build, with the tie published beside the model.
GPU inference on shared hardware: a CUDA decoding engine in 2.7 GiB on the card a 30B model already uses, serving a burst of 2,048 simultaneous clients with none failed.
author: Corey James
